'''Simon Ellingsen''' is an Executive Director of the International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research ([[International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research|ICRAR]]) and is based at the [[University of Western Australia]] node.

== Education ==
Ellingsen attended [[University of Tasmania]], located in [[Hobart, Tasmania]], where he received a [[Bachelor's degree]] ([[First-class honours]]) in 1991. He went on to obtain a [[PhD]] in 1996, with the thesis "Class II Methanol Masers in Star Formation Regions"<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Class II methanol masers in star formation regions|url=https://eprints.utas.edu.au/19640/|publisher=University of Tasmania|date=1996|degree=phd|language=en|first=Simon Peter|last=Ellingsen}}</ref>

== Career ==
Ellingsen is best known for his work on [[star formation]] and the structure of the [[Milky Way]], particularly through observations of methanol [[Astrophysical maser|masers]]. Notable contributions include the first unbiased search for 6.7&nbsp;GHz methanol [[Astrophysical maser|masers]], which identified a large number of previously unknown regions of high-mass star formation,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ellingsen|first1=S. P.|last2=von Bibra|first2=M. L.|last3=McCulloch|first3=P. M.|last4=Norris|first4=R. P.|last5=Deshpande|first5=A. A.|last6=Phillips|first6=C. J.|date=1996-05-11|title=A survey of the Galactic plane for 6.7-GHz methanol masers -- I. l = 325 -335; b= - 0Formula53-0Formula53|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|language=en|volume=280|issue=2|pages=378–396|doi=10.1093/mnras/280.2.378 |arxiv=astro-ph/9601016|issn=0035-8711|doi-access=free}}</ref> discovery of a number of new interstellar methanol [[Astrophysical maser|maser]] transitions<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ellingsen|first1=S. P.|last2=Sobolev|first2=A. M.|last3=Cragg|first3=D. M.|last4=Godfrey|first4=P. D.|title=Discovery of Two New Class Ii Methanol Maser Transitions in G 345.01+1.79 |date=2012-11-01|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/2041-8205/759/1/L5|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=759|issue=1|pages=L5|doi=10.1088/2041-8205/759/1/L5|arxiv=1209.5744 |bibcode=2012ApJ...759L...5E |issn=2041-8205|hdl=10995/51230|s2cid=118344109 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> and the demonstration that class II methanol [[Astrophysical maser|masers]] trace a very early phase of high-mass star formation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ellingsen|first=S. P.|date=2006-02-10|title=Methanol Masers: Reliable Tracers of the Early Stages of High‐Mass Star Formation|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1086/498673|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|language=en|volume=638|issue=1|pages=241–261|doi=10.1086/498673 | arxiv=astro-ph/0510218 |bibcode=2006ApJ...638..241E |s2cid=13889056 |issn=0004-637X}}</ref>  He has used observations of methanol absorption to help constrain changes in the [[proton-to-electron mass ratio]] and made the first detection of extragalactic class I methanol and HC<sub>3</sub>N [[Astrophysical maser|masers]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ellingsen|first1=Simon|last2=Voronkov|first2=Maxim|last3=Breen|first3=Shari|date=2011-12-29|title=Practical Limitations on Astrophysical Observations of Methanol to Investigate Variations in the Proton-to-Electron Mass Ratio|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.270801|journal=Physical Review Letters|language=en|volume=107|issue=27|article-number=270801|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.270801|pmid=22243297 |issn=0031-9007|arxiv=1111.4708|bibcode=2011PhRvL.107A0801E |s2cid=28086251 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ellingsen|first1=S. P.|last2=Voronkov|first2=M. A.|last3=Breen|first3=S. L.|last4=Lovell|first4=J. E. J.|title=First Cosmological Constraints on the Proton-To-Electron Mass Ratio from Observations of Rotational Transitions of Methanol |date=2012-03-01|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/2041-8205/747/1/L7|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=747|issue=1|pages=L7|doi=10.1088/2041-8205/747/1/L7|issn=2041-8205|arxiv=1201.5644|bibcode=2012ApJ...747L...7E |s2cid=118465837 }}</ref> toward [[Sculptor Galaxy|NGC253]]. He continues to work as a researcher at the [[University of Tasmania]].

Ellingsen has contributed to efforts to locate the [[Wow! signal]] with American data analyst, astronomer, and author [[Robert H. Gray]]. In 1998 Ellingsen and [[Robert H. Gray|Gray]] conducted searches using the 26-meter dish at the [[Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory]] in [[Hobart, Tasmania]]. [[Robert H. Gray|Gray]] and Ellingsen made six 14-hour observations where the Big Ear was pointing when it found the [[Wow! Signal]]. [[Robert H. Gray|Gray]] and Ellingsen published "A Search for Periodic Emissions at the Wow Locale" in the October 2002 issue of The Astrophysical Journal, reporting on searches for the Wow! signal.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gray|first1=Robert H.|last2=Ellingsen|first2=Simon|date=2002-10-20|title=A Search for Periodic Emissions at the Wow Locale|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|language=en|volume=578|issue=2|pages=967–971|doi=10.1086/342646|bibcode=2002ApJ...578..967G |issn=0004-637X|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Ellingsen had a number of roles at the [[University of Tasmania]]. Ellingsen has been involved in running research facilities and associated projects at [[The University of Tasmania]] for many years, most recently a Space Infrastructure Fund grant<ref>{{Cite web|title=Supporting space infrastructure growth|url=https://www.industry.gov.au/funding-and-incentives/supporting-space-infrastructure-growth|publisher=Department of Industry, Science, Energy and Resources|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211010025638/https://www.industry.gov.au/funding-and-incentives/supporting-space-infrastructure-growth|archive-date=2021-10-10}}</ref> to construct a new satellite tracking antenna at the [[Greenhill Observatory]].<ref name="Profile">{{Cite web |date=2012-04-16 |title=Simon Ellingsen - Profiles |url=https://www.utas.edu.au/profiles/staff/chemistry/simon-ellingsen |access-date=2021-04-16 |publisher=University of Tasmania, Australia |language=en-AU}}</ref> Ellingsen was appointed as a lecturer in physics in 2000, promoted to senior lecturer in 2005, to Associate Professor in 2010 and to Professor in 2015.  He was Head of Discipline for Physics from 2015 – 2019, becoming Acting Head of School for the School of Natural Sciences in July 2019<ref name="Profile"/> and was appointed to the position of Dean of Natural Sciences in November 2020. In April 2024 he commenced as the Executive Director for the International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research ([[International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research|ICRAR]]) and is based at the [[University of Western Australia]] node.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICRAR welcomes new Executive Director |url=https://www.uwa.edu.au/news/article/2024/april/icrar-welcomes-new-executive-director |access-date=2024-04-09 |website=www.uwa.edu.au |language=en}}</ref>
